assumptions: The training set chosen (eukaryotic or prokaryotic) matches the protein's origin.
limits: Predicts WHERE a cut would fall, not WHETHER the protein is secreted.
A 1986 matrix, not a trained modern predictor.
bio.jane/contract.question: Where would signal peptidase cut this protein, by von Heijne's weight matrix?

description: Signal-peptidase cleavage sites in a protein, by von Heijne's (1986) weight matrix as implemented by EMBOSS sigcleave. Scores a 15-residue window at every position (the 13 residues before the cut plus the first two after) against either the eukaryotic or the prokaryotic training set. Predicts WHERE the cut would fall, not WHETHER the protein is secreted — a high score away from the N-terminus is a look-alike, not a secretion call.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

kingdom.description: which of von Heijne's training sets to score against: 161 aligned eukaryotic or 36 prokaryotic signal peptides. Pick the one matching the EXPRESSION HOST — the two disagree by several points on the same sequence.

minWeight.description: report sites scoring strictly above this. EMBOSS's default of 3.5 finds ~95% of real signal peptides and rejects ~95% of non-signal sequences.

protein.description: the protein sequence (unambiguous one-letter codes); wire it from translate_sequence.

name: protein_signal_peptide

cleavageAfter.description: 1-based residue the best site cuts after; the mature chain starts at the next one. 0 when nothing cleared the threshold

matrix.description: which training set was used, and how many peptides it was built from

maturePeptide.description: the predicted mature chain, from the cleavage site to the end

score.description: the best site's score — a sum of 15 log-odds, NOT a probability

scores.description: the score at every position, thresholded or not — the series a plot draws

siteCount.description: how many sites cleared the threshold

sites.description: every site above the threshold, best first: { cleavageAfter, score, start, end, window, maturePeptide }
